title: STF's Victor AI project: OCR text layer in production since December 2020 (10 million+ pages by May 2021); document splitter and theme classifier still pending in August 2021
summary: STF–UnB Victor: OCR layer live since Dec 2020 (10m+ pages by May 2021); splitter and repercussão geral classifier not yet in production (STF, 19 August 2021); time savings were projections.
account: Victor is a Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) and Universidade de Brasília (UnB) partnership. It began at the end of 2017 under Chief Justice Cármen Lúcia. It was designed to read extraordinary appeals and identify the most frequent repercussão geral themes. Its four tasks: converting images to text, splitting documents, classifying the main procedural documents and identifying repercussão geral themes. On 30 August 2018 Cármen Lúcia announced it was in operation, with tests on 27 themes and a claimed triage precision of 84%. She said work taking a clerk three hours would take five seconds. On 23 October 2018 Chief Justice Dias Toffoli spoke at a CNJ-reported seminar. He said it did in five seconds what cost a clerk 40 minutes to an hour, with 85% accuracy. The STF's own status report of 19 August 2021 states that only the optical character recognition (OCR) layer was effectively implemented. It ran from the end of December 2020 for extraordinary appeals and agravos, with over 10 million pages processed by May 2021. The splitter and classifier were still being put into production with no set date. The theme indication is always validated by the ministers. No measured time saving or case outcome was published; the successor tool VitorIA (2023) is recorded separately.
purpose: Speed up admissibility analysis of extraordinary appeals by flagging the repercussão geral theme that applies. The production OCR layer is a precondition for that, not the classification itself.
system: Victor (STF–UnB artificial-intelligence project: OCR, document splitter, document classifier, repercussão geral theme classifier)
developer: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) with the Universidade de Brasília (UnB)
deployer: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Secretaria de Gestão de Precedentes
taxonomy_note: Only the OCR layer is in production, and the time savings claimed for triage are projections.

ratings.reason: OCR of 10 million pages is a throughput figure, not a measured saving, and the classifier was not in production.
No effect on case backlog or litigants is documented.

ai_role.statement: By the STF's own account of 19 August 2021, the AI classifier that would flag repercussão geral themes was not in production. The only live component was automatic OCR of incoming appeals, which the STF frames as part of the Victor project. Any theme indication is validated by the ministers. The time savings announced in 2018 (three hours or 40 minutes to five seconds) were forecasts made by chief justices at launch. All cited sources are the deployer's news service (STF) and the CNJ, which the same chief justice presided. No independent evaluation was found.

headline: STF's Victor OCR processes 10 million+ pages; classifier pending
metric: more than 10 million pages processed by May 2021

comparator.against: a court clerk converting image files to text by hand
comparator.quote: A ministra ressaltou que o trabalho de conversão de imagens em texto, por exemplo, que um servidor executa em três horas, será feito em cinco segundos com a nova ferramenta.

later.note: In May 2023 the STF said it still operated Victor for repercussão geral triage of incoming appeals, alongside Rafa, while finishing tests of the new VitórIA tool.
later.quote: Atualmente, o STF opera dois robôs – o Victor, utilizado desde 2017 para análise de temas de repercussão geral na triagem de recursos recebidos de todo país, e a Rafa, desenvolvida para integrar a Agenda 2030 da ONU ao STF, por meio da classificação dos processos de acordo com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) definidos pelas Nações Unidas.
